DR-ROBUSTNESS MARGIN (this candidate's own reason to exist): trained under widened mass/contact_stiff/kv+vel/latency/com_offset ranges vs slew_smooth_s0's narrower (identity-only) always-on set -- see cfg_recipe_walk50hz_fs_bisect_drv_safewiden6_acq1.py for the exact verbatim widened values. KNOWN BEHAVIORAL LIMITATION -- DIFFERENT SHAPE FROM slew_smooth_s0, not identical: the composed rise+hold->walk full-heading panel (8 headings x2 episodes, this cycle) shows this checkpoint's RAW (rot60 off) baseline ALREADY clears gait_valid 16/16 with 0 falls at every heading, unlike slew_smooth_s0's own baseline (11/16, failing h+-90/h135/h-135) -- the wider DR training this bundle exists for appears to have also reduced (not eliminated) the chronic off-forward leg-sacrifice signature. However, dist_m at h135/h180/h-135 drops to 0.03-0.42m in the raw baseline (near-stationary) vs 0.65-1.02m at on-axis headings -- a real off-axis PROGRESS penalty that gait_valid alone does not catch. The rot60 wrap (zero retrain, same checkpoint) removes this too: dist_m at those same headings rises to 0.77-0.95m, matching the on-axis band, with 0/16 falls either way. Read as: rot60 remains a real, free-lunch improvement on this checkpoint's off-axis PROGRESS even though the raw leg-sacrifice/gait_valid failure mode it was built to fix does not manifest as sharply here.
